Header: Bidens pilosa Inyabarasanya (Kinyarwanda); Piquant noir, herbe aiguille (French); Blackjack (English)

Prevention: Use clean/certified crop and pasture seed to reduce risk of contamination
Seeds are spread on clothes and shoes - remove seeds when leaving an infested area
Ensure farm equipment/tools are cleaned after use in infested areas to reduce risk of spreading seeds of the weed
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: soya beans, peas
Look for erect broadleaved weed (up to 1m high) with green compound leaves; white flowers with yellow centre and 1cm long black seeds with 2-4 yellowish awns at one end
Check fields twice a month for the level of infestation and growth stage of the weed to guide decision on control before flowering and/or seed setting
Direct Control: Uproot / pull out the weed, allow it to dry and decompose or feed it to livestock (e.g. rabbit)
A maize-bean intercropping system can effectively suppress the weed
Restrictions: Herbicides are not cost effective and environmental friendly for affected crops when grown for subsistence, as is the case in
